_note: Reference data for Digital Twin model verification/validation. Hand-transcribed from the cited sources; no value here is FIREWISE output. There is no calibration set: no model parameter is fitted.

datasets.source: U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976 (NOAA, NASA, USAF), sea-level values
datasets.independence: Not independent of Model A: the standard atmosphere density is itself defined through the ideal-gas law. Used for VERIFICATION only.
datasets.uncertainty: Tabulated to 5 significant figures (±0.00005 kg/m³ rounding).

datasets.source: U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976, composition of dry air at sea level (mole fractions); mean molar mass 28.9644 g/mol
datasets.independence: Verification of the mixture molar-mass sum with the four species FIREWISE represents (Ne, He, Kr, Xe and other trace gases omitted).
datasets.uncertainty: Omitted trace species total about 0.003 mole %.

datasets.source: NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, 4th ed. (Chase 1998): ideal-gas Cp at 298.15 K
datasets.independence: The NASA polynomials are fits to evaluated data of this kind; the comparison VERIFIES coefficient transcription and fit quality at 298.15 K.

datasets.source: White, F. M., Viscous Fluid Flow, 3rd ed. (2006), Table 1-2: Sutherland law for AIR, mu0 = 1.716e-5 Pa·s, T0 = 273 K, S = 111 K (±2% over its stated range)
datasets.independence: Independent of the model under test: the model mixes N2, O2, Ar and CO2 pure-component data with the Wilke rule; the reference is a separate fit to measured air viscosity.

datasets.source: White, F. M., Viscous Fluid Flow, 3rd ed. (2006), Table 1-3: Sutherland-type law for AIR, k0 = 0.0241 W/(m·K), T0 = 273 K, S = 194 K (±2% over its stated range)
datasets.independence: Independent of the model under test (Mason–Saxena mixture of pure-component conductivities).
